title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Opioid overdose
decisions.scenario: A patient is found unresponsive in bed with very slow, shallow respirations. On assessment, the pupils are pinpoint, and the patient does not respond to verbal stimuli or light physical stimulation.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelWhy: Respiratory depression is the immediate threat.

decisions.title: Medication non-adherence
decisions.scenario: A patient with bipolar disorder admits they stopped taking their prescribed medication because they felt “normal again” and believed they no longer needed treatment. The patient appears confident in this decision and minimizes past symptoms.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Explore reasons for non-adherence and provide education.

decisions.title: Antipsychotic extrapyramidal symptoms
decisions.scenario: A patient taking antipsychotic medication begins to exhibit muscle stiffness, tremors, and slowed movements. The patient complains of feeling uncomfortable and restless, with noticeable rigidity in the neck and arms.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess for extrapyramidal symptoms and notify the provider.

decisions.title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
decisions.scenario: A patient receiving antipsychotic medication develops a high fever, severe muscle rigidity, confusion, and autonomic instability. Vital signs are abnormal, and the patient appears acutely ill.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Stop the medication and initiate emergency care.

decisions.title: Major depressive episode
decisions.scenario: A patient reports persistent sadness, extreme fatigue, and loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities for several weeks. The patient speaks slowly, appears tearful, and reports difficulty sleeping and concentrating.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess for suicide risk and initiate therapeutic communication.

decisions.title: Eating disorder – anorexia nervosa
decisions.scenario: A patient diagnosed with anorexia nervosa refuses meals and presents with a markedly low body weight. Vital signs reveal bradycardia, and the patient insists they are “not hungry” and do not need to eat.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess medical stability and enforce meal plan.

decisions.title: Bulimia nervosa
decisions.scenario: A patient reports episodes of binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting. The patient expresses shame about these behaviors and complains of sore throat and fatigue.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess for electrolyte imbalance and dental erosion.

decisions.title: Postpartum psychosis
decisions.scenario: A woman who recently gave birth reports hearing voices that instruct her to harm her newborn. She appears confused, emotionally labile, and disconnected from reality while holding the baby.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Ensure safety of mother and infant and notify provider immediately.
decisions.modelWhy: Postpartum psychosis is a psychiatric emergency.
decisions.trap: Leaving the infant alone with the mother.
